target_customer: Small and mid-sized businesses in Chile and Latin America that pay suppliers and employees
problem: Latin American companies reconcile bill payments, local transfers and expenses by hand across banks and ERPs. Cardda bundles payments, cards and ERP sync.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus card and payments fees
product_category: Fintech, spend management and B2B payments

founders.name: Cristóbal Grinbergs
education: Universidad de Chile, civil industrial engineer
previous_startups: Rentz (heavy-equipment rental marketplace, reached breakeven per YC page, pivoted into Cardda June 2020)
founders.background_notes: DF article of January 2022 gives his age as 27; recorded only in notes, not as age_at_founding.

investors: Unnamed pre-YC investor (7 percent stake per DF)

competitors.name: Brex
competitors.what: US corporate card and spend platform named by the founders as a reference

competitors.name: Ramp
competitors.what: US corporate card and spend management, named in the same article

competitors.name: Clara
competitors.what: Mexican LatAm corporate cards, B2B payments and expense platform
competitors.traction_then: Launched March 2021, later reached unicorn status in about eight months per press
competitors.funding_then: 3.5M USD pre-seed led by General Catalyst in March 2021

competitors.name: Mendel
competitors.what: Mexican spend management for LatAm enterprises
competitors.funding_then: 35M USD debt and equity in December 2021

competitors.name: Pleo
competitors.what: European spend management cards, named in DF article

competitors.name: Spendesk
competitors.what: European spend management platform, named in DF article

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs bank and tax authority integrations, ERP connectors and card issuing partnerships in several countries, which is standard fintech engineering with regulatory and integration friction.

defensibility.rationale: ERP syncs and payment workflows create some lock-in, but well-funded rivals (Clara, Mendel, Kapital) were entering the same market.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Funded LatAm rivals moved first; Cardda remained small and in August 2025 announced expansion to Peru. No acquisition by 2026.

market_need_then: Founders argued most company spend in Latin America flows through transfers and bill payments, not only cards; the DF article (January 2022) cites reconciliation pain, and card-led spend startups were raising money in 2021.

branding.domain_note: Uses exact cardda.com per YC page and company site

identity.voice_and_tone: Business-like Spanish language site, 'más de 350 empresas confían' proof style

branding.community_and_virality: Press mainly Chilean business outlets (DF, 2022 and 2025); no sign of merch or community.

brand_strength.rationale: The name suggests cards but the double d is a likely misspelling source, and no brand-driven growth was found.

pivots.why: Pivot made during the pandemic per DF and YC page

outcome_analysis: Cardda pivoted out of an equipment rental marketplace into LatAm spend management in 2020, joined YC in Winter 2022 and reports 350 plus client companies and a Peru launch in 2025. Funding stayed small (about 330K USD reported by the founders at YC time), while Clara and Mendel raised far more in the same niche, so growth looks capital-efficient but modest. No exit or shutdown found.
notes: The DF article (January 2022) says founders raised about 330K USD in total from angels, Start-Up Chile, Platanus Ventures and YC. The 100K USD for 7 percent is recorded as a round with no date; YC's standard 125K USD deal is not recorded as a round. Aggregators disagree (CB Insights 720K USD, VCBacked 500K USD); not recorded as rounds. Cardda site does not name founders.
